title: 2026 Half-Year Report
gist: Glencore's H1 2026 results show an $10.1bn Group Adjusted EBITDA (+86%) and a swing to $4.4bn net income, driven by a Middle East conflict that repriced oil, refined products, LNG and freight and delivered a near-record $3.3bn Marketing Adjusted EBIT (+142%). Management pairs c.$1.5bn of fresh returns (8.5c/share special plus a $500m buyback) with a c.$19.7bn illustrative FY26 EBITDA, a copper path to c.1Mt by end-2028, and a newly announced ASX secondary listing targeted for October 2026.

themes.theme: Middle East conflict repriced the energy complex

insights.claim: Glencore says H1 2026 was defined by a significant repricing of energy and closely related markets after an escalation of the Middle East conflict, which flipped the year from a well-supplied energy complex to a scramble for security of supply and physical access.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Confirms the 2026 commodity rally is a physical-availability shock, not demand-led — favours holders of physical inventory and optionality over pure price beta.
insights.quote: H1 2026 was characterised by the significant repricing of energy and closely related markets and risks, following escalation of the Middle East (ME) conflict.
insights.locator: Gary Nagle CEO comment — 'H1 2026 was characterised by'

insights.claim: Constraints across oil, refined products, LNG and freight capacity drove heightened volatility across global energy and other markets in H1 2026, according to Glencore.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Freight and refined-product bottlenecks, not just crude, are the transmission channel — watch tanker rates and crack spreads as the leading indicator of trader P&L.
insights.quote: Constraints across oil, refined products, LNG and freight capacity, drove heightened volatility across global energy and other markets.
insights.locator: Gary Nagle CEO comment — 'What began the year as a relatively'

insights.claim: The Middle East conflict caused supply-chain disruptions that materially hit the availability and pricing of key mining consumables — specifically diesel, sulphur and sulphuric acid — pushing Glencore's operating costs above normal inflationary levels.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Second-order: an energy shock raises miners' unit costs with a lag, so copper/nickel producers without integrated energy exposure face margin compression even in a price upcycle.
insights.quote: materially impacting the availability and pricing of key inputs and consumables (e.g. diesel, sulphur and sulphuric acid) beyond normal inflationary considerations
insights.locator: Gary Nagle CEO comment — 'The Industrial segment contributed'

insights.claim: A generally weaker US dollar was cited by Glencore as a headwind that partially offset the benefit of stronger commodity prices in its Industrial segment during H1 2026.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Dollar weakness inflates local-currency mining costs — a reminder that FX can claw back a meaningful slice of a commodity price upcycle for producers with non-USD cost bases.
insights.locator: Gary Nagle CEO comment — 'These benefits were partially offset'

insights.claim: Glencore's Group Adjusted EBITDA rose 86% period-on-period to $10.1 billion in H1 2026, from $5,430 million in H1 2025, against full-year 2025 of $13,511 million.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: A single half now nearly matches all of 2025's EBITDA — the operating leverage in a diversified trader/miner to a physical supply shock is enormous.
insights.quote: Group Adjusted EBITDA increased 86% to $10.1 billion, while Net income attributable to equity holders increased by more than $5 billion period on period to $4.4 billion.
insights.locator: Gary Nagle CEO comment — 'Against this backdrop, Group Adjusted EBITDA'

insights.claim: Glencore swung from a $655 million loss attributable to equity holders in H1 2025 to $4,405 million of income in H1 2026, with basic EPS moving from US$(0.05) to US$0.37.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: A >$5bn swing in six months resets the earnings base — consensus models anchored to 2025's $0.03 full-year EPS are stale.
insights.locator: Key statement of income and cash flows highlights table

insights.claim: Glencore reported Adjusted EBIT of $6,651 million in H1 2026 versus $1,801 million a year earlier, a 269% increase and above the $5,978 million recorded for the whole of 2025.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: EBIT grew far faster than EBITDA (269% vs 86%), showing fixed D&A amplifying the price move — operating leverage is even steeper below the depreciation line.
insights.locator: Key statement of income and cash flows highlights table

insights.claim: Glencore's H1 2026 revenue reached $174,430 million, up 49% from $117,396 million, versus $247,535 million for full-year 2025.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: H1 revenue is already ~70% of the prior full year — top-line run-rate implies a step change in working capital and financing needs for commodity traders.
insights.locator: Key statement of income and cash flows highlights table

insights.claim: Funds from operations at Glencore rose 158% to $8,129 million in H1 2026 from $3,147 million, approaching the $8,714 million generated across all of 2025.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Cash conversion, not just accounting earnings, inflected — this is what funds the buyback and special distribution announced alongside.
insights.locator: Key statement of income and cash flows highlights table

insights.claim: Glencore's H1 2026 net income attributable to equity holders of $4.4 billion exceeded the $3.7 billion pre-significant-items figure, with the difference driven by gains on disposals of non-current assets, recognition of deferred tax assets and impairments.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: About $0.7bn of the headline profit is non-recurring/below-the-line — use $3.7bn as the clean base when extrapolating.
insights.quote: Net income attributable to equity holders, pre-significant items: $3.7 billion; Net income attributable to equity holders: $4.4 billion, reflecting gains on disposals of non-current assets, recognition of deferred tax assets and impairments
insights.locator: 2026 HALF-YEAR FINANCIAL SCORECARD

themes.theme: Marketing desk and the diversified-trader model

insights.claim: Glencore's Marketing Adjusted EBIT was $3.3 billion in H1 2026, up 142% period-on-period and described by the company as a near record H1 result, driven by materially disrupted energy, freight and other markets.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: The trading arm is effectively a long-volatility, long-dislocation position — it re-rates hardest exactly when macro risk spikes, providing a natural hedge inside a mining portfolio.
insights.quote: Marketing Adjusted EBIT of $3.3 billion, up 142%, a near record H1 result, owing to the materially disrupted energy, freight and other markets during the period
insights.locator: 2026 HALF-YEAR FINANCIAL SCORECARD

insights.claim: Glencore frames its marketing, logistics and risk management capabilities as the mechanism that converts geopolitical uncertainty into earnings by efficiently sourcing, transporting and delivering physical energy and metals when supply is constrained.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: A reusable model: in physical-shortage regimes, value accrues to control of logistics and optionality rather than to reserves in the ground.
insights.quote: This environment continues to highlight the value of the Group's marketing, logistics and risk management capabilities, enabling us to efficiently source, transport and deliver essential energy and metals products
insights.locator: Gary Nagle CEO comment — 'Marketing Adjusted EBIT was $3.3 billion'

insights.claim: Marketing contributed roughly a third of Glencore's H1 2026 profitability, with $3.3 billion of Marketing Adjusted EBIT alongside $6.5 billion of Industrial Adjusted EBITDA within a $10.1 billion Group Adjusted EBITDA.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Investors valuing Glencore purely on mining multiples understate the earnings mix — the trading stream carries a different (and more volatile) multiple.
insights.locator: 2026 HALF-YEAR FINANCIAL SCORECARD

insights.claim: Glencore describes itself as a producer and marketer of more than 60 commodities with over 140,000 employees and contractors and a footprint in over 30 countries, also providing financing, logistics and other services to producers and consumers of commodities.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: The breadth of commodities plus an embedded financing/logistics arm is what lets a single energy shock translate into group-wide upside — a structurally different exposure from a single-commodity miner.
insights.locator: Notes for Editors

insights.claim: Glencore's Industrial segment delivered Adjusted EBITDA of $6.5 billion in H1 2026, up 72% period-on-period, primarily reflecting higher commodity prices with assets performing in line with market guidance.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: The Industrial uplift is price-driven, not volume-driven — meaning it fully reverses if the ME-driven price shock unwinds.
insights.locator: 2026 HALF-YEAR FINANCIAL SCORECARD

insights.claim: Glencore disclosed H1 2026 Adjusted EBITDA mining margins of 52% for copper, 38% for steelmaking coal and 19% for energy coal.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: A clean margin ranking: copper earns nearly triple the margin of energy coal, quantifying why capital is being redirected to copper growth rather than coal.
insights.quote: Adjusted EBITDA mining margins were 52% for copper, 38% for steelmaking coal and 19% for energy coal
insights.locator: 2026 HALF-YEAR FINANCIAL SCORECARD

insights.claim: Energy coal's 19% Adjusted EBITDA margin at Glencore is the weakest of its three disclosed mining margins, sitting well below copper's 52%, even in a half characterised by an energy price shock.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Counterintuitive: an energy crisis did not restore thermal coal economics to copper-like levels — challenges the 'coal is the cash cow' thesis for Glencore.
insights.locator: 2026 HALF-YEAR FINANCIAL SCORECARD

themes.theme: Balance sheet discipline and capital returns

insights.claim: Glencore operates an explicit ordinary-course net debt cap of about $10 billion, and reported net debt of $10.2 billion at 30 June 2026 after a $1.0 billion reduction during the half — i.e. right at its self-imposed ceiling.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: The cap is the binding constraint on distributions: cash above it goes to shareholders, so returns are mechanically predictable from net debt versus $10bn.
insights.quote: Net debt, having declined by $1.0 billion during the period, is in line with our ordinary course of business net debt cap c.$10 billion.
insights.locator: Gary Nagle CEO comment — 'After making our regular proforma adjustments'

insights.claim: Glencore's net debt fell $1.0 billion to $10,194 million despite $4.0 billion of net capital expenditure, $1.9 billion of non-RMI net working capital build and $1.1 billion of shareholder distributions during H1 2026.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Deleveraging while spending $4bn on capex and paying out $1.1bn shows the cash engine can fund growth and returns simultaneously at current prices.
insights.locator: BALANCE SHEET

insights.claim: Glencore's net debt to Adjusted EBITDA ratio fell to 0.56x at 30 June 2026 from 0.83x at end-2025, a 33% reduction, on a last-12-months EBITDA basis.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Sub-0.6x leverage in a cyclical peak gives ample headroom for counter-cyclical M&A or larger buybacks if prices hold.
insights.locator: Key financial position highlights table

insights.claim: Glencore's net funding rose 8% to $42,418 million from $39,405 million, which the company attributes primarily to higher energy and metals prices inflating the value of Readily Marketable Inventories held at period end.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Gross funding growth here is price-driven inventory financing, not balance-sheet deterioration — the standard trap when screening traders on gross debt.
insights.quote: primarily reflecting the impact of higher energy and metals prices on our Readily Marketable Inventories held at period end
insights.locator: BALANCE SHEET

insights.claim: Glencore held $14.0 billion of available committed liquidity at the half-year and maintains a policy of capping bond maturities at no more than about $3 billion in any given year.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Laddered maturities plus $14bn of committed liquidity is the structural defence against a margin-call/refinancing squeeze in volatile physical markets.
insights.quote: Available committed liquidity of $14.0 billion; bond maturities maintained around a cap of no more than c.$3 billion in any given year
insights.locator: BALANCE SHEET

insights.claim: Glencore's net debt figure includes $1,208 million of Marketing-related lease liabilities at 30 June 2026, up from $1,010 million at end-2025.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: A definitional detail worth normalising when comparing Glencore's leverage against peers who exclude marketing leases.
insights.locator: Footnotes to key financial position highlights

insights.claim: Glencore's total assets grew 9% to $155,447 million and total equity 10% to $36,812 million between end-2025 and 30 June 2026.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Equity growth roughly tracks asset growth, confirming the balance sheet expansion is retained earnings and inventory value rather than gearing up.
insights.locator: Key financial position highlights table

insights.claim: Glencore announced a top-up special cash distribution of 8.5 US cents per share (about $1.0 billion) plus a new $500 million share buyback to be completed by February 2027, lifting total announced 2026 shareholder returns to about $3.5 billion.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: A concrete c.$1.5bn incremental return with a defined February 2027 buyback completion date — a mechanical bid under the shares through to early 2027.
insights.quote: we announce today a top-up special cash distribution of $8.5c/per share (c.$1 billion), alongside a new $500 million share buyback to be completed by February 2027
insights.locator: Gary Nagle CEO comment — 'After making our regular proforma adjustments'

insights.claim: Glencore explicitly treats its Bunge shareholding as surplus capital and, consistent with prior practice, converts that stake's value into special cash distributions to shareholders.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: A repeatable playbook: non-core listed stakes are treated as distributable rather than strategic — watch for further Bunge-linked top-ups as the stake is monetised.
insights.quote: Consistent with prior practice, recognising our Bunge shares as surplus capital
insights.locator: Gary Nagle CEO comment — 'After making our regular proforma adjustments'

themes.theme: Copper growth pipeline running ahead of schedule

insights.claim: Glencore reaffirms it is well positioned to reach annualised copper production of about 1 million tonnes by the end of 2028, and a target of about 1.6 million tonnes by 2035.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: A ~60% copper volume growth path from 2028 to 2035 makes Glencore a primary listed vehicle for structural copper demand — key benchmark to track against project milestones.
insights.quote: we remain well positioned to reach copper production volumes of c.1 million tonnes annualised by the end of 2028 and our c.1.6 million target by 2035
insights.locator: Gary Nagle CEO comment — 'In terms of asset development'

insights.claim: The Alumbrera restart is running ahead of schedule, with first production now expected in H2 2027 versus original guidance of H1 2028 — a roughly two-quarter pull-forward.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Rare positive schedule revision in mining; pulls copper cash flows forward and de-risks the 2028 1Mt milestone.
insights.quote: Some, including the Alumbrera restart, are running ahead of schedule, with its first production now expected in H2 2027 compared to original guidance of H1 2028.
insights.locator: Gary Nagle CEO comment — 'In terms of asset development'

insights.claim: A substantial part of Glencore's increase in net cash purchase and sale of PP&E to $4.0 billion in H1 2026 (from $3.2 billion) comprises copper portfolio investments to secure land access supporting growth and operational flexibility.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Buying land access, not just plant, signals long-dated copper expansion optionality — and explains capex outrunning maintenance needs.
insights.quote: substantial part of the increase comprises copper portfolio investments to secure land access to support growth and operational flexibility
insights.locator: 2026 HALF-YEAR FINANCIAL SCORECARD

insights.claim: Glencore says it is making good progress across the various projects presented at its December 2025 Capital Markets Day, with some running ahead of schedule.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: The December 2025 CMD project slate is the reference document for tracking delivery against management's growth promises.
insights.locator: Gary Nagle CEO comment — 'In terms of asset development'

themes.theme: ASX secondary listing and the Australian capital pool

insights.claim: Glencore intends to apply for a secondary listing on the ASX via CDIs, targeting admission in October 2026, following a detailed review of ways to broaden its investor base and enhance trading liquidity.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: A dated catalyst: index inclusion and Australian institutional buying around an October 2026 admission could structurally lift the shareholder register and liquidity.
insights.quote: we intend to apply for a secondary listing on the ASX, targeting admission in October 2026
insights.locator: Gary Nagle CEO comment — 'We are also announcing today'

insights.claim: Glencore cites Australia's A$4.4 trillion pension asset pool, expected to grow to approximately A$12.4 trillion by 2045, as a core rationale for listing on the ASX.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Roughly a tripling of Australian pension assets over ~20 years is a structural bid for ASX-listed resource equities — relevant well beyond Glencore.
insights.quote: Australia is home to one of the world's largest and fastest-growing pools of long-term investment capital, with A$4.4 trillion in pension assets expected to grow to approximately A$12.4 trillion by 2045.
insights.locator: Gary Nagle CEO comment — 'An ASX secondary listing (via CDIs)'

insights.claim: Glencore argues Australian investors' access to diversified copper exposure has diminished following industry consolidation and M&A activity in recent years, positioning its ASX listing to fill that gap.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Scarcity of ASX-listed diversified copper is the pitch — implies a possible scarcity premium for Glencore CDIs and for remaining local copper names.
insights.quote: it would provide increased access to diversified copper exposure at a time when local investment opportunities have diminished following industry consolidation and M&A activity in recent years
insights.locator: Gary Nagle CEO comment — 'An Australian listing is also expected'

insights.claim: Beyond liquidity, Glencore expects an Australian listing to strengthen its profile in one of its most important operating jurisdictions and to enhance corporate financial flexibility.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Regulatory/social licence and financing flexibility in Australia are unstated-but-real drivers — relevant given Glencore's coal and copper assets there.
insights.locator: Gary Nagle CEO comment — 'An Australian listing is also expected'

themes.theme: Full-year 2026 guidance implies a softer H2

insights.claim: Glencore has calculated an illustrative full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of about $19.7 billion, based on current commodity prices and an expected uplift in H2 volumes, particularly for steelmaking coal.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: An explicit management-anchored FY number roughly 46% above 2025's $13.5 billion — the benchmark against which H2 results and consensus should be judged.
insights.quote: we have calculated a full year 2026 illustrative Adjusted EBITDA of c.$19.7 billion
insights.locator: 2026 HALF-YEAR FINANCIAL SCORECARD

insights.claim: Glencore's c.$19.7 billion illustrative full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA implies roughly $9.6 billion in H2 against $10.1 billion delivered in H1, i.e. a modestly lower second half despite guided volume growth.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Management is implicitly assuming some mean reversion in marketing/energy prices — a spot-price-flat H2 with higher volumes would beat the illustrative figure.
insights.locator: 2026 HALF-YEAR FINANCIAL SCORECARD

insights.claim: Steelmaking coal is singled out by Glencore as the commodity driving an expected H2 2026 volume uplift, making it the key swing factor for hitting full-year guidance.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Track steelmaking coal shipment volumes as the highest-signal operational KPI for a guidance beat or miss.
insights.quote: Based on current commodity prices and an expected uplift in H2 volumes, particularly for steelmaking coal, we anticipate continued strong cash generation through the remainder of 2026.
insights.locator: 2026 HALF-YEAR FINANCIAL SCORECARD
